raw.title: Principal Product Manager (Content Authoring, Delivery & CMS)
raw.excerpt: Who We AreGreat Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007.
raw.description:
Who We Are

Great Minds is a high-growth, mission-driven organization founded by educators in 2007. As a for-profit, Public Benefit Corporation, we believe all students deserve access to meaningful, challenging content—and all teachers deserve tools that are intuitive, effective, and built for the realities of today’s classrooms.

We develop high-quality, knowledge-rich math, science and ELA curricula grounded in research and designed in collaboration with educators. Our materials reflect real classroom needs and are built to drive lasting student outcomes.

We are committed to usability, coherence, and practical implementation—supporting teachers not just through curriculum, but with professional learning, purposeful technology, and responsive service that enable strong adoption and impact.

What We Build

Our products—Eureka Math and Eureka Math², Wit & Wisdom, PhD Science, Geodes, and the newly launched Arts & Letters ELA—are trusted by thousands of schools and districts nationwide.

  • Eureka Math is the most widely used math curriculum in the U.S., and is focused on balancing conceptual understanding, procedural fluency, and application.

  • Wit & Wisdom® and Arts & Letters ELA™ anchor our reading strategy with content-rich, grade-level instruction that integrates literature, history, and the arts, grounded in the science of reading. Geodes® complements our reading suite with decodable texts that pair phonics with meaningful content to support early literacy.

  • PhD Science is a hands-on K-5 Science program that sparks curiosity as students build enduring knowledge of how the scientific world works.

These programs reflect a shared belief in high expectations, joyful rigor, and deep respect for educators and students.

Where We’re Headed

Great Minds is entering a new stage of growth and product maturity. We are focused on building more connected, customer-informed experiences across the full educator journey—from curriculum to professional learning to platform and support.

Our long-term vision is to become a true partner in impact—not just delivering curriculum, but supporting educators in achieving outcomes at scale.


Job Purpose

Reporting to the Director, Digital Product Management, the Principal Product Manager (Content Authoring, Delivery & CMS)will lead discovery and execution for our content authoring tools, end user delivery experiences, and content management system (CMS). This role will be critical to how curriculum and assessment content is created, managed, and experienced by teachers, students, administrators, and internal teams. This is a top-level individual contributor role with broad ownership and influence. The position will work with product design, engineering, curriculum, and assessment teams to ensure Great Minds’ authoring and delivery platforms are coherent, scalable, and deeply supportive of high-quality K–12 instructional and assessment experiences. The role will partner closely with Product Design, Engineering, and other teams in and outside the Digital department.


Responsibilities

  • Content Authoring Platforms:

    • Define and evolve the product vision for tools used to author curriculum and assessment content.

    • Balance usability for authors with structural rigor required for downstream delivery, analytics, and interoperability.

    • Partner with curriculum and assessment teams to translate instructional intent into scalable software capabilities.

  • End User Content Delivery:

    • In partnership with the Chief Technology Officer, directors, and other leaders, form product strategy for how authored content is delivered to teachers, students, and administrators.

    • Ensure delivery experiences are performant, accessible, intuitive, and instructionally sound.

    • Work closely with Digital Product Design to validate real classroom and instructional workflows.

  • CMS and Content Architecture:

    • Initiate and sometimes facilitate product direction conversations for the CMS, including content models, workflows, permissions, versioning, and publishing—working with but deferring to expert partners in Product Design and Engineering.

    • Ensure the CMS supports multiple products, grade levels, subjects, delivery contexts, and modalities.

    • Partner with Engineering on long-term platform scalability and maintainability.

  • Responsibilities:

    • Set clear product strategy and success metrics for authoring, delivery, and CMS capabilities.

    • Translate complex instructional and operational needs into well-scoped product initiatives.

    • Write clear roadmap proposals and product requirements when they are defined.

    • Collaborate deeply with Product Design to ground decisions in user needs and evidence.

    • Partner with Engineering to make sound trade-offs across speed, quality, and technical health.

    • Influence roadmap priorities in partnership with Product Management and leadership.

    • Act as a subject matter expert on content platforms for Great Minds commercial products.

    • Identify and reduce friction across the content lifecycle—from creation to classroom use.

Are you a socially conscious, dedicated individual who is committed to building a better future for children, families, and their communities? If so, join us as we support early childhood education programs across the country to create positive outcomes for the children and families served.

About the Acelero Charitable Foundation

The Acelero Charitable Foundation exists to promote futures of infinite promise for children everywhere. Rooted in the belief that every child deserves access to high-quality early learning and strong family support, the Foundation invests in people, practices, and policies that drive meaningful change in the early childhood ecosystem. Our grantmaking spans research, direct support to families and educators, and initiatives that expand access to excellent early education across Public Systems.

We are seeking a Founding Executive Director to help bring our vision to life as we enter an exciting new chapter with a refined strategic direction and expanded philanthropic aspirations.

The Opportunity

As the Foundation’s first staff leader, the Founding Executive Director will play a pivotal role in building and stewarding a values-aligned, high-impact organization. You will launch and lead the Foundation’s strategic, fundraising, and grantmaking work, while managing essential operations. This is a rare opportunity to shape the identity and impact of a foundation with bold ambitions and deep roots in early childhood education.

What You'll Do
Strategic Leadership & Organizational Development

  • Lead implementation of the Foundation’s strategic framework.

  • Serve as the primary liaison to the Board of Directors; support governance, board development, and committee operations.

  • Build the internal systems and infrastructure needed for strong grantmaking, evaluation, and public transparency.

Fundraising & External Partnerships

  • Design and execute a diversified fundraising strategy targeting individual donors, major gift prospects, institutional funders, and public agencies.

  • Cultivate and steward relationships with philanthropic partners aligned to our mission.

  • Manage donor reporting and communications; ensure high standards of transparency and accountability.

Grantmaking & Program Oversight

  • Lead and evolve the Foundation’s grantmaking in three core investment areas.

  • Funding and publishing early childhood research.

  • Expanding access to high-quality early education across Public Systems.

  • Providing direct support to children, families, and educators.

  • Establish application processes, review committees, performance tracking, and grantee learning communities.

  • Provide high-level oversight and strategic guidance for all grant-funded initiatives.

  • Monitor overall grant portfolio performance, identifying key trends and areas for strategic intervention.

Evaluation, Learning, & Communications

  • Drive a research & learning agenda that prioritizes field insights, grantee voice, and continuous improvement.

  • Produce an annual public Impact Report focused on advancing quality early learning.

  • Represent the Foundation in the field and amplify research findings through thought leadership and collaborative initiatives

Who You Are

  • Strategic and entrepreneurial: You love building from the ground up and have a track record of scaling impact.

  • Passionate about early childhood equity: You bring a deep commitment to children, families, and the power of early education.

  • Experienced fundraiser: You know how to build relationships, write compelling proposals, and steward major gifts.

  • Nonprofit-savvy: You understand 501(c)(3) governance, public benefit requirements, and ethical grantmaking.

  • 7+ years of leadership experience in philanthropy, nonprofit management, or policy.

  • Demonstrated success in fundraising and external engagement.

  • Deep knowledge of early childhood systems and/or family engagement strategies strongly preferred.

  • Strong communication, organizational, and project management skills.

  • Comfort navigating ambiguity and building new processes.

When/Where/How Much:

  • This is a part-time, fully remote position, with an estimated 20–25 hours per week.

  • Compensation will be commensurate with experience and competitive with similar foundation roles (part-time $66,000 - $100,000).

If you are ready to pair strategy with mission driven values, apply today and join the Acelero Charitable Foundation.

- Career growth and professional development opportunities

- Supportive working environment

- Average of 5 weeks of paid time off during 1st year of employment

raw.description:
The Digital and Marketing Technology Manager owns two closely related areas.

Digital marketing: website content, user journeys and performance; email campaigns and the firm newsletter (currently Mailchimp); social media, primarily LinkedIn; Google Analytics and digital reporting; Semrush and search performance; and campaigns across digital channels.

Marketing technology: administration and optimization of Lawmatics and Lawbrokr; implementation and optimization of CallRail and Voice Assist; website forms and platform connections; system testing, documentation and user training; and the quality of marketing and intake data together with the dashboards built on it.

Dashboards in scope are digital, marketing and intake. Firm-wide reporting that combines financials, matters and operations sits outside this role.

The Director retains oversight of strategy, priorities, brand, budget and overall performance. This role owns day-to-day delivery and manages the specialist agencies for Google Ads, website design and development, and complex platform connections.

The role is measured on its contribution to pipeline rather than on activity alone. Signed matters depend on factors beyond marketing, including lawyer availability, conflicts, pricing and engagement decisions, so what is measured is the contribution to and quality of the pipeline rather than sole accountability for what closes.

This is a different profile from a traditional Digital Marketing Manager. We are looking for someone who has led implementations, designed workflows and resolved problems, rather than someone who has used the platforms. This is a significant hire and the process reflects that: it includes a practical exercise as well as interviews.

  • Build the function, not just operate it: Help shape Taxpayer Law’s emerging marketing technology ecosystem and establish the processes that will support its next stage of growth.
  • Own technology that directly drives revenue: Connect digital marketing, automation, analytics, intake technology, and agency performance to a measurable pipeline and signed matters.
  • High-impact role with real autonomy: Work closely with leadership in a growing, modern law firm where your technical judgment, execution, and improvements will have visible business impact.

Agency management and paid media

•Manage the specialist agencies day to day (Google Ads, website design and development, and complex platform connections): prepare briefs, review results critically, and, with the Director's support, hold each agency accountable within the Director's strategy and budgets. Conduct structured reviews using Google Analytics, Semrush and other relevant performance data, and support agency audits, comparisons and transitions.

•Supervise the PPC agency across Google Ads (Search and Performance Max) against cost-per-qualified-lead targets; spend is roughly CA$30K per month. With the Director's support, QA exclusions, invalid traffic controls, conversion signals, landing page alignment and lead quality. A meaningful share of paid leads are currently unqualified and improving this is a priority for the role. This requires someone able to challenge an agency on substance, not simply manage the relationship.

•Test approved emerging digital channels in conjunction with specialist agencies, including appropriate opportunities presented by AI platforms.

Marketing technology

•Administer and optimize Lawmatics and Lawbrokr; build and maintain connected website forms and platform connections across the stack; manage system testing, documentation, user training and the quality of marketing and intake data; and build and maintain the agreed digital, marketing and intake dashboards. Functional ownership of these platforms continues after implementation and covers configuration, optimization, documentation, testing and user support.

•Clio Grow is in scope only where it supports intake, lead source data, pipeline reporting or marketing technology connections. Clio Manage, matter administration, billing and legal practice workflows are out of scope.

•Implement and optimize CallRail and Voice Assist, including the enhanced Voice Assist pilot. The Director and the Marketing and Intake Coordinator define the business and client experience requirements and assess performance; this role owns technical configuration, testing and reporting.

•Potential future scope, not a first-year commitment: if the firm proceeds with a CRM, lead the assessment and implementation, then own CRM data, workflows, automation and reporting. Marketing, business development and intake would define the requirements and business case; firm leadership would approve the investment and the ownership model.

Newsletter, email and website

•Establish and manage delivery of the firm newsletter (currently Mailchimp): audience building across clients, accountants and referral sources; template development and cadence; deliverability and list growth. Assemble each issue from Head of Thought Leadership content and firm news, editing and packaging rather than writing substantive tax content. Newsletter content planning sits within Marketing Programs; this role owns the delivery end.

•Run mailing campaigns and follow-up communications around webinars and launches, and the digital promotion for awards and survey campaigns.

•Manage website content, user journeys, performance and the delivery roadmap. Supervise the web developer on changes beyond the SEO program, and own the Lawbrokr lead capture relationship.

•Implement approved privacy requirements such as cookie consent and tracking disclosures. The firm's privacy position is established through firm governance with appropriate legal and technical advice; this role implements what has been approved rather than determining the position.

•Support the Director in leading the planned website project and manage the agency relationship. The Director leads the project and defines brand, audiences, content strategy, client journey, scope and priorities. This role develops and manages the delivery plan, coordinates the agency, oversees analytics, search requirements, forms and platform connections, manages testing and supports launch. Specialist providers deliver user experience, visual design and technical build.

•Ensure the firm retains ownership and administrative control of its domain, hosting, analytics and other critical website accounts.

Reviews, social and webinars

•Own the client review program, comprising automated post-matter NPS surveys with lawyer safeguards and Google review invitations, and keep the Google Business Profile current. Client satisfaction policy is set by the Director.

•Manage the LinkedIn company page and YouTube channel. Adapt, package and publish content supplied by the Head of Thought Leadership, the Marketing Programs Manager, human resources and other relevant contributors, including repurposing webinars, presentations and articles into posts and clips. Commission freelance creative and video production where required.

•Manage the webinar platform, registration, promotion, email automation, recording, follow-up and performance reporting in accordance with the firm playbook. Coordinate dry runs and technical delivery. Partner with the Marketing Programs Manager and the Marketing and Intake Coordinator on content and logistical support; partner organization relationships sit with the Marketing Programs Manager.

Reporting and operations

•Verify agency tracking and attribution (GA4, CallRail, offline conversions); monitor search performance through Semrush; maintain lead source data quality across Lawmatics and Clio Grow; track digital vendor spend against the marketing budget.

•Prepare the digital performance report for the Director's monthly marketing call. Report the funnel stage by stage (click, inquiry, consultation, signed matter) and flag conversion leaks, such as slow response to leads, for discussion with the Director and intake.

Must have

•Fluent English, written and spoken.

•Five or more years across both digital marketing and marketing technology, including three or more years of management-level accountability for digital channels and marketing systems. You have led platform implementations, designed workflows and resolved problems, not simply used the platforms.

•Experience supervising PPC or digital agencies to results, with the ability to audit an account and its reporting rather than take vanity metrics at face value.

•You have built or run an email newsletter, with list growth, deliverability and engagement you can speak to with numbers, and you are comfortable hands-on in ad, email and marketing platforms.

•Analytics fluency (GA4, call tracking, CRM data) sufficient to verify tracking and reporting, and clear plain-English writing for emails, ads and web pages.

•Evidence of succeeding in a growing and comparatively less structured organization. You are comfortable working through ambiguity, developing practical processes and operating without extensive specialist support.

Strongly preferred

•An international law firm or comparable professional services environment, ideally tax or accounting.

•Lawmatics, Lawbrokr, CallRail, Clio Grow or comparable platforms, and CRM selection or implementation experience.

•Review generation and local presence programs (NPS, Google Business Profile); webinar production and YouTube growth; AI search visibility and AI advertising platforms. French is an asset.

About the Company

Our client is a leading provider of business software solutions (ERP, HCM, CRM, BI) in Romania and one of the top 10 global software providers for the leasing industry. Their flagship products, Charisma ERP and Charisma HCM, are market leaders, serving businesses across financial services, retail, distribution, production, construction, agriculture, medical, and service industries. With projects in 45 countries and a growing international footprint, they continue to innovate and expand globally.

About the Role

We are looking for a Information Security Officer (ISO) to implement the cybersecurity strategy, ensuring the protection of both internal systems and customer data. This role involves developing and implementing security policies, conducting audits and compliance certifications, and driving strategic initiatives in information security. The ISO will report to the Chief Risk and Compliance Officer and work closely with cross-functional teams to ensure security and regulatory compliance.

Responsibilities

  • Lead internal InfoSec projects and drive strategic security initiatives
  • Develop and implement security policies and procedures for the organization and its software delivery teams
  • Conduct security analyses, audits, certifications, and re-certifications for compliance with ISO 27001, NIS, SOC, and other international InfoSec standards
  • Provide customized cybersecurity consulting and solutions for clients
  • Monitor national and European cybersecurity regulations and implement proactive strategies to ensure compliance
  • Collaborate with internal teams to assess security risks and develop mitigation strategies

Required Skillset

  • Minimum 2-3 years of experience in a similar InfoSec leadership role
  • Strong expertise in developing and executing security strategies aligned with industry best practices
  • Experience in risk assessment, compliance frameworks, and cybersecurity governance
  • Excellent communication skills in English and Romanian, with the ability to engage at all organizational levels
  • Analytical mindset, strong problem-solving skills, and attention to detail
  • Ability to work creatively and proactively in a problem-solving environment

raw.description:
ADMINISTRATIVE ASSISTANT ;

A remote admin job may be a good option if youre looking for a career that allows you to work from home and manage your hours. But what is a remote admin job, exactly? And what skills do you need to succeed in this career field?

A remote admin job generally refers to any administrative work that can be done remotely, such as data entry, customer service, or scheduling. Many businesses are now looking for employees who can do these tasks from their home office, as it can save the company money on overhead costs and attract a larger talent pool. If you have these skills and are interested in working from home, a remote admin job may be an excellent option.

What Is an Administrative Job?

Within the role of administrative support, the tasks can vary greatly depending on the field and the business or professional you are supporting. At its core, however, an admin job involves tackling routine tasks required for companies to function.

With technological advances, many admins can now work from home, as they can answer phone calls, tap into company software and documents, and interact with coworkers from their home office.

What Industries Can You Work in as an Admin?

A role in administration is an excellent choice for anyone wanting the flexibility of career mobility between industries. You can pursue a field that aligns with your interests and passions, and you will have the opportunity to learn new skills and knowledge.

The best part about a career in administration is that you can work in various industries, including healthcare, education, business, and government. In addition, you can find employment opportunities in both the private and public sectors. Whether youre looking for a job in a large corporation or a small business, theres sure to be an administrative role right for you.

Is an Administrative Job Right for You?

If youre considering a career in remote administration, there are a few key traits that will help you succeed:

Self-motivation: When working remotely, getting sidetracked or becoming bogged down with distractions can be easy. Staying on task and maintaining a good work-life balance is essential.

Organizational skills: As an admin, youll likely juggle multiple tasks and deadlines. Staying organized and prioritizing your work will be critical to your success.

Communication skills: Since youll often be the first contact that other employees and the public have with a company or executive, its crucial to have strong communication skills. This includes effectively communicating via email, phone, and over video.

Technical skills: Regardless of your industry, you will need essential technical skills to work effectively from home. However, if you dont have these skills, there are often training programs available to help you get up to speed.

Admin Job Description: What Does an Admin Do?

In a remote admin job, the specialist is responsible for supporting an executive, a team or department, or an entire business. Depending on the scope of the role, this can include scheduling appointments, handling correspondence, and managing social media accounts.

The duties of a remote admin vary depending on the specific needs of the individual or team they are supporting. However, some everyday duties are typically included in most admin positions, such as:

Answering and routing phone calls

Scheduling appointments and meetings

Handling correspondence

Managing social media accounts

Preparing reports

Providing customer service

Maintaining files and records

Processing payments

Booking travel arrangements

How to Become a Remote Admin

There are many different career paths you can take as a remote administrator, and many entry-level positions are available without a formal degree. You could move into management or become a specialist in a particular area (such as managing an executives schedule and travel arrangements).

Some admin professionals have used their experience to grow their freelance careers by focusing on bookkeeping, email, or social media management careers. If youre interested in moving up within the field of remote administration, here are some things to keep in mind:

Experience in multiple administration areas will make you more marketable and better equipped to oversee managerial duties.

Pursuing a degree or certification in business administration can help you stand out from other candidates and give you the skills and knowledge needed to pursue leadership roles.

Networking with other professionals in the field is a great way to get your foot in the door.

Creating Work-Life Balance With a Remote Admin Role

If youve determined that a remote admin role is a great fit, use the following tips for success as you launch your remote career.

Set regular hours and stick to them. Setting boundaries will help you avoid working long hours and prevent burnout.

Make time for wellness every day. Whether taking a walk, reading a book, or taking a yoga class, carving out some me time will help you relax and recharge.

Stay connected with friends and family. Working remotely can be isolating, so staying connected with your loved ones is essential.

Get out of the house. Working from home can be great, but getting out once in a while is essential. Take advantage of the time youre saving by not commuting and visit new places, go on hikes, or check out that restaurant youve been meaning to try.

Invest in a good work setup. A comfortable and ergonomic workspace will help you be more productive and efficient when working from home. Make sure your desk is at the right height, your chair is comfortable, and you have enough light.

Take breaks throughout the day. Just because youre working from home doesnt mean you must be glued to your desk all day long. Get up and stretch, take a walk, or grab a snack. Taking breaks will help you stay focused and avoid burnout.
